articles.heading: General Provisions for Arbiter Titles
articles.content:
FIDE awards two arbiter titles:
- FIDE Arbiter (FA)
- International Arbiter (IA)

Both titles are awarded for life unless revoked by the FIDE Ethics and Disciplinary Commission. Once awarded, a title cannot be downgraded except as a disciplinary sanction.

Candidates must:
- Hold a FIDE ID
- Be a member of a national federation affiliated with FIDE
- Demonstrate knowledge of the Laws of Chess, FIDE regulations, and practical arbiting experience
- Apply through their national federation

The FIDE Arbiters' Commission (ARB) administers the arbiter title system and maintains the list of all FAs and IAs worldwide. Title applications are reviewed and approved by ARB before being forwarded to the FIDE Council.

An arbiter must not apply for a title for which they do not qualify. False applications are subject to disciplinary action.

articles.heading: Arbiter Norms
articles.content:
An arbiter norm is a performance credit awarded for serving as an arbiter at a qualifying event. Norms are graded by the category of event:

Norm Categories:
- Category A: Olympiad, World Championship (Open/Women/Junior/Senior/Youth), Continental Championship (Open/Women)
- Category B: Continental Championship (Junior/Youth/Senior), FIDE Grand Prix, Zonal Championships (Group 1)
- Category C: Zonal Championships (Groups 2-5), National Championships in large federations, other qualifying international events
- Category D: Qualifying events at national level

Norms accumulate over a career. The number and category of norms required for each title are specified in B06.1.3 (FA) and B06.1.4 (IA).

For a norm to be valid:
- The arbiter must have served in an official capacity (Chief Arbiter, Deputy Chief Arbiter, or arbiter)
- The event must be registered with FIDE or the relevant Continental Federation
- The norm report must be submitted within the required time frame
- The arbiter must have performed their duties satisfactorily

articles.heading: Requirements for the FIDE Arbiter Title
articles.content:
To be awarded the FIDE Arbiter (FA) title, a candidate must satisfy ALL of the following:

1. Pass the FIDE Arbiter seminar examination with a score of at least 80%

2. Accumulate the required number of arbiter norms from qualifying events. The norm requirements are updated periodically by ARB — candidates must check the current requirements on the FIDE website.

3. Demonstrate sufficient knowledge of the Laws of Chess and tournament regulations.

4. Possess a FIDE ID.

5. Have the application endorsed by their national federation.

Note on the examination: The FIDE Arbiter seminar exam tests knowledge across all areas covered by the Arbiters' Manual, including the Laws of Chess, Swiss and Round Robin systems, rating regulations, title regulations, and practical arbitering scenarios. A score of 80% is required to pass.

A candidate who fails the examination may retake it at the next available seminar. There is no limit on the number of attempts, but a fee is charged for each seminar attendance.

articles.heading: Requirements for the International Arbiter Title
articles.content:
To be awarded the International Arbiter (IA) title, a candidate must satisfy ALL of the following:

1. Already hold the FIDE Arbiter (FA) title

2. Demonstrate proficiency in at least one FIDE official language (English, French, Spanish, Russian, German, Arabic, Portuguese)

3. Accumulate the required number of arbiter norms from international qualifying events. IA norms require higher-category events than FA norms.

4. Have served as Chief Arbiter or Deputy Chief Arbiter at qualifying events.

5. Have the application endorsed by their national federation.

The IA title requires demonstrating competence at high-level international events. The FIDE Arbiters' Commission may interview candidates for the IA title to verify their experience and knowledge.

For arbiters based in countries where FIDE official languages are not native, language competency may be demonstrated through activity at international events where such languages are used.

articles.heading: Application Procedure for Arbiter Titles
articles.content:
The application procedure for arbiter titles:

1. Norm reports: For each qualifying event, the organiser or Chief Arbiter completes an FA1 (FIDE Arbiter Norm Report Form) or IA1 (International Arbiter Norm Report Form) and submits it to FIDE through the national federation.

2. Title application: When the candidate has accumulated sufficient norms and passed the examination, the national federation submits FA2 (Application for award of the title of FIDE Arbiter) or IA2 (Application for award of the title of International Arbiter).

3. Review: ARB reviews the application at its next meeting. Applications may be submitted online through the FIDE website.

4. Fee: The applicable application fee must be paid before the title is awarded.

5. Publication: Approved titles are published on the FIDE website and in the next available FIDE rating list.

Financial regulations: Fees for seminars, norm reports, and title applications are specified in the FIDE Financial Regulations. Fees are subject to change by FIDE Council decisions.

articles.heading: FIDE Regulations for the Training of Chess Arbiters
articles.content:
FIDE Arbiter seminars are organised by FIDE, continental federations, and national federations under FIDE's supervision.

Seminar requirements:
- Must follow the FIDE-approved curriculum (based on the Arbiters' Manual)
- Must be conducted by FIDE-accredited lecturers (FIDE Lecturers — FL)
- Must include at least the minimum number of teaching hours required by ARB
- Must include a written examination
- Must be registered with FIDE in advance

FIDE Lecturer accreditation:
- To become a FIDE Lecturer (FL), a candidate must be an IA and attend an FL training programme
- FLs are accredited by the ARB and must teach at least one seminar every four years to remain active

Lecturers Training Programme:
- FL candidates must attend a specific FIDE Lecturer Training Programme
- The programme covers teaching methodology, examination techniques, and updated regulations

Seminar examination:
- Consists of multiple-choice and scenario-based questions
- Covers all sections of the Arbiters' Manual
- A score of at least 80% is required to pass
- Results are submitted to FIDE for verification
- Candidates who fail may retake the exam at the next available seminar

articles.heading: Classification of Arbiters
articles.content:
Active FAs and IAs are classified into categories based on their level of activity and the events they have officiated. Classification is managed by the FIDE Arbiters' Commission.

Categories of IAs:
- Category A: Arbiters who have served as Chief Arbiter or Deputy Chief Arbiter at Level 1 (Olympiad, World Championship) events
- Category B: Arbiters who have served at Level 2 (Continental Championship) events
- Category C: Arbiters who have served at Level 3 (Zonal, national championship) events
- Category D: All other active IAs

Activity requirements:
- An arbiter must serve at a minimum number of events per year (or per four-year cycle) to remain active in their category
- An arbiter who fails to meet activity requirements is downgraded to the next lower category or to 'inactive' status
- Inactive arbiters retain their title but are not listed in the active category register

Application for classification upgrade:
- Applications for category upgrade (e.g. from Category C to B) must be submitted through the national federation using Form IA3
- The ARB reviews upgrade applications and approves or rejects them based on the applicant's activity record

articles.heading: Appointment of Arbiters in World Events
articles.content:
Arbiters for FIDE World Events are selected by panels maintained by the FIDE Arbiters' Commission under the oversight of the relevant FIDE commissions (EVE, GSC).

Appointment requirements for World Events:
- The Chief Arbiter must typically be a Category A IA
- Deputy Chief Arbiters must be Category A or B IAs
- Arbiters must not have a conflict of interest with any participant
- Arbiters from the federations of competing players must be carefully assessed for potential conflicts

Panels:
- ARB maintains four appointment panels (Panels 1-4) with arbiters classified by their experience and category
- Panel 1 contains the most experienced arbiters (eligible for World Championship)
- Appointments to World Championships and Olympiads come from Panel 1

Limitations on appointments:
- An arbiter may not serve at more than a specified number of top events per cycle
- An arbiter with a known conflict of interest must recuse themselves

Appointment to World events is considered the highest honour in arbiting. Arbiters appointed to such events represent the profession and are expected to maintain the highest standards of conduct and impartiality.

articles.heading: FIDE Arbiter Disciplinary Regulations
articles.content:
The ARB Disciplinary Sub-Committee (ARB-DSC) handles complaints against arbiters.

Jurisdiction: The ARB-DSC has jurisdiction over all FAs and IAs in matters related to their arbiting duties. Complaints must be submitted to the ARB-DSC with supporting evidence.

Offences (Article 3 of B06.5) include:
- Serious errors in applying the Laws of Chess or FIDE regulations
- Misconduct or behaviour unbecoming of an arbiter
- Failure to follow FIDE anti-cheating regulations
- Corruption or manipulation of results
- Failure to submit required reports
- False statements in norm or title applications

Sanctions (Article 4 of B06.5) available:
1. Warning (formal written warning)
2. Suspension from arbiting for a specified period
3. Downgrading of classification category
4. Suspension of the arbiter title
5. Revocation of the arbiter title

All sanctions are subject to appeal to the FIDE Appeals Committee. Serious offences may be referred to the FIDE Ethics and Disciplinary Commission (EDC), which has the power to impose bans from chess activities more broadly.

Procedural rules ensure that the accused arbiter is informed of the complaint, given an opportunity to respond, and has the right to representation.
